recipes.name: Broccoli Cheddar Soup
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds processed cheese food (eg. Velveeta), cubed

steps.text: Bring broth to a simmer in a large pot over medium heat. Cook broccoli in simmering broth for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a separate skillet over medium heat, melt margarine. Add onion and sauté for 5 minutes, or to desired tenderness. Stir flour into onion until pasty. Gradually add milk and stir until thick.
Add onion mixture to broccoli mixture in the pot and stir well. Stir in cheese until melted; do not boil. Season with white pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli Cheddar Soup
raw_recipe.description: Broccoli cooked in chicken broth is combined with milk, processed American cheese, and onion sautéed in margarine to create a rich soup popular with children.

review.reviewBody: This is a very good recipe you can tweak. I have made it quite a few times. Unless you LOVE Velveeta, I would highly recommend using half cheddar cheese (otherwise your soup will taste more like Velveeta cheese dip). I always use 1 pound of velveeta and 1/2 - 3/4 pounds of cheddar and I always end up with restaurant quality soup. Also, remember to constantly stir the milk mixture "until it thickens" and you will have a nice and smooth, thickened soup. I do not use white pepper but put in a dash of regular pepper. Substituting a good portion of the velveeta with cheddar makes a great tasting, quality soup. My family loves it - even my three kids. I rate this 5 stars with the addition of cheddar. If I rated this using all Velveeta then the rating would have been 1 star.

This soup is fantastic. I am watching calorie intake, so I reduced the Butter to 4 Tbsp. and the cheese to 8 oz. Velveeta and 6 oz. Cheddar. Added some black pepper and a bit of granulated garlic. I also used an immersion blender on the broccoli/broth mixture after it was done cooking, before adding the flour mixture. Turned out great. Will definitely be my go to recipe for Broccoli Cheese soup.

Guests for dinner tonight and there were lots of compliments for this soup around the dinner table! I did make some changes that I believe were improvements - butter rather than margarine for its superior flavor, fresh broccoli rather than frozen (cooked easily and lickety-split in the microwave) a clove of garlic and a mix of 2/3 Velveeta and 1/3 Cheddar. I cooked the broccoli in advance and set it aside. Sweated the onion in butter, added the garlic, then the broth and milk. Once it thickened just a little I lowered the heat and slowly stirred in the cheeses, then gently stirred in the broccoli. Excellent soup - creamy, rich and satisfying. Since we're leaving town again, our guests were only too happy to have the leftovers.

Wait. Why? Just why??? Would anyone use fake processed cheese. I used sharp Cheddar. Also, I did not simmer the broccoli separately. I sautéed the onions and garlic in half butter half olive oil. Then added broccoli and chicken stock. Brought to boil and simmered 15 mins. Then pureed in blender. Next add milk and heat to just before boiling. (Used oat milk) finally, turn off burner and add cheese. Delicious! Served with homemade Naan.

Very good basic recipe however I made some changes for personal preferences. Omitted onions using sauteed garlic in butter until translucent then adding flour stirring until thickened and bubbly. Added 4c.water with 4 tsp. Maggi chicken bouillon granules, 1c. half & half, 2c. 2%milk and 1 can condensed cream of mushroom soup. Heated thoroughly then added 10oz. frozen steamable, microwaved broccoli followed by 8 oz. hickory smoked ham, cubed, 8oz. Med. Cheddar cheese.

This turned out wonderful. I substituted a pound and a half of real cheddar for the Velveeta and just mixed it in very slowly, a little at a time, at the end with the heat turned off. I had no trouble and it turned out creamy and delicious. Thanks!

I save the bottom tougher part of the broccoli and freeze it when I cook the florets. When I have enough, I use it to make soup. This is the first time I made this particular recipe, but I did not have chicken broth so I substituted watered down beef broth. I use my immersion blender when the soup is well cooked. The outcome was delicious. I also used sharp cheddar cheese and put grated Parmesan cheese on top when I served it. Hubby was pleased and I served it with crusty bread.

This is a wonderful recipe, and any changes that I made are for health reasons or because I needed to because I didn't have some things in my pantry. It was so easy to make and the best broccoli soup I've ever made. Because of a recent dental surgery, I did find that the broccoli was a bit hard, so when I make it again, and I will make it again, I will boil it in the broth for a bit or just cut the broccoli up more before cooking. I also only had one pound of Velveeta so I put that plus 3/4 pound of sharp cheddar. Lastly, I'm from Louisiana where we put Tony's seasoning in EVERYTHING so I added this instead of pepper. I'm sure pepper would have been just fine. Thank you for the amazing recipe!

I love this recipe but I did follow some reviewers' recommendations. I used 1 lb. Velveeta and 1/2 lb. sharp cheddar and I was very careful not to let the soup come to a boil. I also added a large clove of garlic, minced, to the onion but not sure that added anything. At the end I added some red pepper because my family likes spice. The best overall tip was to add the cheese to the onion mixture, which I did in portions, and stir to melt, and then add to the broccoli. I think this was an excellent tip. I served with warm ham slices and artesian style bread. My boys loved this and it made a LOT so leftovers for the weekend. Thanks!

Ruined the broccoli for Christmas dinner so salvaged it with this soup. Agree with doubling the cheese. Used Velveeta to ensure an even melt. A little sharp cheddar would probably enhance the flavor. I used 1% milk but would use 1/2 and 1/2 next time. I did not have enough cornstarch so I made a roux of an equal amount of flour. Thickness good, but flour leaves a slight after taste. Next time I would use cornstarch. I love garlic but did not think it enhanced this soup. I would omit. The recipe does make a lot of soup. Enough for 10 servings at least.

Excellent recipe - such a satisfying, comforting soup! As others suggested, I sauteed some garlic with the onions and added one diced potato withe the broccoli. Also, I use American Cheese from the deli - prefer the taste over the shelf-stable block type. I used both white and yellow American cheese along with some cheddar. Great texture and flavor.
I made this soup but used chicken broth(spice) instead of plain.How can i get rid of the spicey taste. Other wise delicious.
It was perfect for my family. Everyone loved it. Added about a 1/2 cup of extra flour after I added the liquid, and I used another 2 cups of chicken broth.
Didn’t think it was as great as others. Didn’t get thick. Onion mixture was very thick, but when added to broccoli, then cheese, it didn’t thicken up. Maybe tomorrow it will be better.
I add some shredded carrot, and use 1pound Velveeta and 8oz Mexican 4-cheese blend.

This was easy to follow. We both loved the flavor and texture. I did use fresh broccoli. Steamed and cut in mostly small pieces, but I did leave some larger pieces for a texture change. Followed the recipe as to cooking. AAA+

I only used 1 large pkg of frozen broccoli but next time I will add some diced carrots also. I used a block (cubes) of Canadian Armstrong Old Fort Cheddar cheese. It melted beautifully. Best soup ever and I have tried other soup recipes. This one is the best. Fast and simple. No need to add any salt.
Great flavor and totally worth the effort my family loved it
Everyone absolutely loves this soup!!!
It was my 1st time ever making this soup and it was a hit!!! Why but it, when I can make it myself? Love this
